bullets.text: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services over the internet.
Services include servers, storage, databases, software, and AI.
It's a model of renting computing resources instead of owning and maintaining them.
Analogy: Paying for electricity without owning the power plant.
On-demand self-service: Users access resources without human interaction.
Broad network access: Services available over the internet from various devices.
Resource pooling: Providers share resources across multiple customers.
Rapid elasticity: Resources scale up or down quickly based on demand.
Measured service: Usage is monitored and billed according to consumption.
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): Provides fundamental computing resources like virtual machines, storage, and networking.
Platform as a Service (PaaS): Delivers infrastructure plus a development platform with built-in tools and frameworks.
Software as a Service (SaaS): Offers ready-to-use applications over the internet (e.g., Gmail, Microsoft 365).
Public Cloud: Services delivered over the internet and shared by multiple organizations.
Private Cloud: Dedicated to a single organization, offering more control and security.
Hybrid Cloud: Combines public and private clouds for balanced flexibility and security.
Community Cloud: Shared by several organizations with common goals or requirements.
Advantages include reduced costs, improved scalability, and enhanced flexibility.
Further benefits are reliability, disaster recovery, and support for innovation.
Challenges include security and privacy concerns for data on remote servers.
Potential for downtime, compliance regulations, and vendor lock-in.
Performance concerns for applications requiring high speed or low latency.
Data storage and backup (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive).
Business collaboration tools (Slack, Microsoft Teams).
Entertainment streaming platforms (Netflix, Spotify).
Healthcare (EHR, telemedicine) and Education (Coursera, Google Classroom).
AI and Big Data analytics for processing large datasets and machine learning.
Edge computing: Data processed closer to the source for reduced latency.
Multi-cloud strategies: Using services from multiple providers to avoid vendor lock-in.
Serverless computing: Developers focus on code, provider manages infrastructure.
Continued focus on security, compliance, and advanced encryption.
Integration with AI, blockchain, and 5G to expand possibilities.
